what_is: WBTC is Wrapped Bitcoin, an ERC-20 token that represents Bitcoin on Ethereum; its public token page is available on Etherscan. Use the official WBTC Network destination to confirm current mint, redemption, merchant, and custody information before moving funds.

how.d: Use the app button to go to wbtc.network, then confirm the domain before connecting a wallet or following any merchant route.
Check whether you need minting, redemption, or receiving existing WBTC; availability can depend on supported providers and jurisdiction.
Confirm WBTC on Ethereum and match the token contract before receiving, swapping, or approving anything.
Follow the official flow, review every wallet prompt, and track the Bitcoin and Ethereum-side confirmations where applicable.

points.p: WBTC is designed so Bitcoin liquidity can interact with Ethereum applications that support ERC-20 tokens.
The WBTC token contract is publicly viewable on Etherscan, which helps users verify the asset before interacting.
Start from WBTC Network and verify the domain, route, and redemption path before sending funds.

faq.a: It means moving from native BTC exposure into a tokenized representation such as WBTC for use in Ethereum applications.

faq.q: Can I wrap btc directly from this page?
faq.a: No. This page routes users to the official WBTC Network destination; verify wbtc.network before connecting a wallet or sending funds.

faq.q: Which token do I receive when I wrap btc?
faq.a: The common Ethereum destination is WBTC, an ERC-20 token; confirm the contract on Etherscan before interacting.

faq.q: Is wrap btc the same as swapping BTC?
faq.a: No. Wrapping creates or uses a tokenized BTC representation on another network, while swapping exchanges one asset for another through a market or liquidity route.

faq.q: What should I check before I wrap btc?
faq.a: Confirm the official domain, token contract, receiving network, wallet prompts, service fees shown in the selected route, and the available redemption path.
